groups.K19: pstack isolates parallel work with Cursor cloud subagents. Its Claude Code map gives each worker a worktree instead, so the guide says that.
groups.K20: huajar-stack runs only Claude models, so the judge and the trail reviewer run on Opus, not on a model from another vendor.
groups.K21: GitHub slugs huajar-stack's heading with its /huajar-stack: prefix, so the link anchor differs from pstack's.
groups.K22: huajar-stack ships deslop itself, so the guide does not send people to another plugin.
groups.K23: Claude Code guidance in place of a Cursor-only feature, or with no Cursor counterpart: /loop as a bundled skill, auto mode allow rules, restarting Claude Code, Claude Code Projects, routines, Desktop scheduled tasks, and the bundled /run and /verify.
groups.K24: The pictures come from pstack and show its command names, so the guide tells people what to type instead.

groups.K27: pstack's text here covers a piece that the map's Left out of huajar-stack table names, so huajar-stack does not ship it: the make-bot-ui skill, or the benny automation pack.
groups.K28: Claude Code's Agent tool takes `effort` as well as `model`, and setup-huajar-stack's rule omits both for `inherit-parent` and `auto`, so pstack's sentence that the subagent `model` field alone is omitted is false here.
groups.K29: huajar-agent's file has no model line. A Cursor slug there would reach the Claude Code API, so the caller passes model and effort on every spawn, as the adapter says.
groups.K30: Windows has no shebangs, Java prints CRLF there, and a folder cannot be renamed over an empty one. So on Windows the command runs a script JAVA with the interpreter its shebang names, passes -Dline.separator to the JVM so TLC's -tool output and its plain output end lines alike, and removes an empty --out before the rename.
groups.K31: On Windows, npm is a .cmd file that runs only through a shell, an ESM import needs a file URL rather than a drive path, a symlink needs Developer Mode while a junction does not, and a folder that TLC just left can refuse removal for a moment, so each folder removal retries. The tests that need POSIX signals, ps -o, or mkfifo skip there.
groups.K32: On Windows, Oracle's java.exe in javapath is a stub whose JVM child can hold its folder for seconds after the stub exits, and fs.rmSync does not retry a removal there. So the command retries a folder removal for up to 22 seconds.
groups.K33: Windows keeps what a test leaves in %TEMP%, Git Bash's ln -s makes links that its sh follows without Developer Mode, and Oracle's java.exe stub can leave its JVM holding a folder for seconds. So each test process keeps its temporary folders in one folder that it removes on exit, the launcher tests on Windows make their links with ln -s and run the launcher with sh, and the tests remove a folder with the command's retrying removeDir.

Write each rule for the shell tool the run uses, `Bash(...)` or `PowerShell(...)`, because one does not cover the other.

In Git Bash, `hc ls --json | jq -r` ends each line with CRLF, so an unstripped `cwd` matches no path.
Then `git worktree remove --force <path>`, and confirm the dir is gone.
